# 099-the-documentation-site — info

*Generated by `104` from the folds in `099-the-documentation-site.lua`. Do not edit this page;
edit the program and run the sweep again.*

**An instrument** — phase 14. Not part of the machine, and it does not ship
to whoever builds one.

## What it is

Builds the whole project as a cross-linked site: every document, blueprint,
companion page and ticket, reachable from every other, with the numbers taken
from the ledger at build time rather than transcribed.

For a general reader: reading this project on disk means holding a
number-to-file mapping in your head, because a hundred and eighty files refer
to each other by number alone -- 037 is a blueprint, 1004 is a ticket, 009 is
a document. On a page every one of those is a link, and every page also says
what points at it, which is a direction nobody can see from inside a file.

Built, never edited. Nothing under docs/HTML/ is a source file and version
control ignores it. The builder is the artifact.

### In the author's words

**`M.run`**

Build the whole documentation site: every document, blueprint, companion page
and ticket in the project as a cross-linked page, with live values from the
ledger and a backlink from everything to everything that mentions it.

Nothing under docs/HTML/ is a source file and none of it is tracked. Every
page is derived from a file already in the repository, and the whole tree
rewrites whenever any dimension changes, so keeping it would put the same
words in the record twice.

**`M.report`**

How many pages were written and where. Deliberately terse: the site is the
output, and a long report about building it is noise in front of the thing
worth looking at.

## What it reads

`091`, `094`. Every instrument here reaches for its dependencies with `dofile`
against a hard-coded project root rather than with `require`, because
there is no package path to configure and a root that can be overridden
by an argument is this project's convention for anything runnable.

## Running it

Both. Something else can load it, and a person can run it:

    luajit src/099-the-documentation-site.lua [project-directory]

---

*Every function in this project is wrapped in a vimfold that opens with a
comment carrying its name, followed by prose, followed by the definition.
That was adopted so a long file collapses neatly in an editor. It is also,
by accident, a machine-readable statement of what a module offers, and it
is the only reason this page can exist — Lua itself says nothing about what
a file exports.*
